title: Dispersion, off-diagonal terms, and stronger distribution
pvg_object: correlations between two valuation/divisibility blocks after principal mass is removed
ant_object: Linnik dispersion method, large-sieve quadratic forms, and off-diagonal bilinear cancellation
forward_translation: Expand averaged residue discrepancies into diagonal and off-diagonal bilinear terms; stronger distribution requires a certificate controlling the off-diagonal correlations.
reverse_translation: A dispersion estimate records aggregate correlation cancellation but does not recover individual valuation profiles or phases.
preserved_information: quadratic average cancellation across moduli or residue fibers
lost_information: pointwise localization and full higher-order dependence
trigger: Mean-square residue errors are available and a stronger level of distribution is sought.
typical_output: an averaged distribution estimate with explicit modulus and bilinear ranges
error_or_wall: Diagonal control alone leaves the load-bearing off-diagonal sum untreated.
required_certificate: Write the expanded quadratic form, isolate diagonal and off-diagonal pieces, and prove the needed bilinear correlation estimate.
positive_example: Small average residue error becomes useful only after the relevant off-diagonal bilinear form is bounded.
counterexample: A variance identity by itself is not a Bombieri--Vinogradov theorem.
anti_overclaim: Dispersion is an analytic cancellation method, not a consequence of geometric relabeling.
classification: Off-diagonal distribution route / bilinear certificate required
source_basis: Classical Linnik dispersion and large-sieve methods
